historical_sanity_anchors: Historical 11th Army captured Changsha 18 Jun, Hengyang airfield 26 Jun, then failed in initial city assaults; supply, heavy-weapons concentration and Fourteenth Air Force interdiction were major constraints.
Historical principal assault divisions at Hengyang were 68th and 116th Divisions.

progress.result: 68th/116th lead the southward rail-river axis while 13th/40th and other elements protect flanks, repair routes and keep the first-echelon traffic from congesting one corridor. Chinese rear guards trade ground for time rather than commit the IX War Area main body.

Japanese leading elements enter the northern/eastern Hengyang operational belt. Chinese 10th-Army-centered defense, reinforced by preserved IX War Area formations, shifts from mobile delay to prepared local defense. High-value stores and air-service equipment begin displacement south.

Methodical fighting reaches the Hengyang airfield/outer-communications system. Japanese forces physically seize most of the airfield complex by 4-5 Jun centerline, but demolition/cratering prevents immediate medium/heavy-air use. Hengyang city and the decisive rail/command node remain Chinese-held.

force_use.Japanese_main_reduction_force: 68th and 116th Divisions centered for the Hengyang reduction problem; supporting divisions secure approaches, flank crossings and LOC rather than all ten divisions entering the city fight.
force_use.Chinese_posture: Preserve the IX War Area field army while making Hengyang a prepared strongpoint. The city garrison is not treated as the entire regional reserve.
force_use.no_bypass_assumption: Hengyang cannot simply be ignored because it is the rail/air/command junction needed for a reliable continuation toward Lingling/Guangxi.

losses_25May_5Jun_working_band.interpretation: Fighting is materially heavier than the Changsha rearguard phase but has not yet become the full urban siege. Chinese force-preservation prevents a large encirclement haul.

Fourteenth_AF_25May_5Jun_effect.effect: Meaningful bridge/rail/river and column interdiction; insufficient to starve the campaign, but enough to make a hasty Hengyang storm materially worse.

decision_5Jun: NO_IMMEDIATE_CITY_STORM. Hengyang is now a methodical reduction/siege problem. Concentrate artillery, engineers and air support, close the local node ring, and reassess after several days rather than extrapolate Changsha tempo.
guards: Hengyang city remains Chinese-held at 5 Jun T24.
Airfield physical seizure is not equal to operational air-base transfer.
